findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P)

Upon arrival to inspection, 5-gal bucket of chlorine sanitizer observed empty. Staff replaced the bucket for a new one. Facility does not have test strips for chlorine (see #48). PIC placed call to Ecolab to order new chlorine strips. In the meantime, facility opted to switch from chlorine to quaternary ammonium sanitizer so they are able to test it and verify it is sanitizing. Inspector re-primed machine with quat sanitizer and strips yielded a concentration of 400ppm. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Facility does not have test strips for chlorine sanitizing dish machine, chlorine was the in-use sanitizer upon inspector arrival. See #16. Facility opted to use quaternary ammonium sanitizer until test strips can be ordered. 

Discussed sanitizing procedures with present staff. Test strips must be on hand at all times for working containers of sanitizers to ensure the concentration is sufficient enough to destroy pathogens. Although the container may be full, a blockage in the lines (for example) could prevent sanitizer from making it onto equipment to be sanitized. Testing the concentration at least once daily via a test strip is the only way to verify sanitizing step is working. 

Follow up issued for test strips. Text/call inspector when received chlorine test strips from Ecolab.

4-602.11(E)(4) The baffle and ceiling inside the ice machine behind the baffle were soiled with mold. Cleaning frequency was discussed with kitchen manager.
 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. Clean and sanitize all components of the ice machine as needed.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 A package of roast beef deli meat was observed with a date mark of 1/2/19 in the walkin cooler. Manager stated that was the day the product was originally opened and frozen. The deli meat was pulled from the freezer yesterday and would be used today. Proper date marking was discussed. Kitchen manager was advised to make sure the date is being marked accordingly when foods are frozen and then changed when products are removed from the freezer for thawing to accurately represent the time frame by which foods are to be used or discarded.  

Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly marked, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

The mop head was being stored in the mop bucket.  Invert mop heads to facilitate quick drying.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
Two cans of apple pie filling were dented on seams.  To correct the violation, the cans were put in the office to be returned to the vender.

750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Two moist wiping cloths were observed on tables.  To correct the violation, the cloths were put in a bucket of sanitizer.

750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
There was a build-up of lime and/or soap on the outside of the dish machine.  Clean the machine.

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Bowls and saucers were stored food side up and uncovered on a set of wire shelves in the dish washing room.  Invert or cover the bowls and saucers.

750-860 Utensils shall be air-dried before being stored or shall be stored in self-draining position.  Glasses and cups shall be stored inverted. Utensils shall be covered or inverted wherever practical. Unless tableware is pre-wrapped, holders for knives, forks, and spoons at self-service location shall protect these articles from contamination and present the handles of the utensils to the consumer.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The counter was soiled with debris behind the coffee machine.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 800e - Observed the vent above the dishmachine to be soiled with dust.  All non-food contact surfaces must be properly cleaned and kept clean to reduce the potential for cross contamination and possible foodborne illness.  Properly clean all non-food contact surfaces.
